result.title: CoRelate: Coordinated Human-Object Motion Synthesis through Interaction Relations
result.summary: Human-object motion synthesis requires coordinated human participation as objects move toward specified goals. However, reaching object targets does not ensure that contact is established and maintained, while adjustments that improve contact may interfere with task completion. We introduce CoRelate, a diffusion framework that coordinates full-body human-object motion through explicit interaction relations and task feedback for rigid and articulated objects. We represent intended participation through hand-part relations that specify the participating hand, its part-relative reference position, and participation interval. These relations serve both as generation conditions and as references for measuring interaction realization. At each denoising step, a temporal refiner trained jointly with the generator combines relation deviations, task residuals, and motion features from the current prediction to jointly update human and object motion across the sequence. After generation, temporal motion correction addresses remaining contact failures by optimizing local motion segments while preserving object trajectories and protected human motion. Experiments demonstrate improved object-goal satisfaction, contact F1, and complete interaction success over the evaluated baselines. Ablation studies support the benefits of relation conditioning and the complementary roles of task and relation feedback.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CoRelate，用一个扩散框架协调生成全身人-物运动：以「手-部件关系」（参与手、部件相对参考位置、参与时间区间）作为生成条件与交互实现程度的度量，并在每个去噪步由联合训练的时间精化器融合关系偏差、任务残差与当前预测的运动特征统一更新人和物体轨迹，生成后再对局部片段做运动修正以缓解残余接触失败。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把任务必要的关系/接触约束写成显式条件，并在生成过程中按偏差反馈逐步更新状态、事后针对失败片段做约束保持的局部纠正，可能为 LVR 的迭代状态更新、证据或关系保真校验与停止/纠正机制提供线索，可供核查该反馈如何进入内部状态而非仅作后处理打分。
